Hi Ellie / Samir —

Thanks again for the kickoff today. Attached is a lightweight navigation map (NSH-implementation-map-v1.xlsx) that lays out the end-to-end handoff we discussed: data export, embeddings generation, index backfill windows, rerank evals, and the canary rollout plan.

High-level notes up front:
- Objective: Replace the current hybrid BM25+heuristics front end with a two-stage flow (ANN candidate retrieval from vector index -> learned reranker). Goal: measurable relevance lift without measurable regressions in latency or CTR.
- Backfill approach we recommend: incremental prioritization by traffic slice (hot queries -> top customers -> long-tail). This lets us warm caches and keep user-facing latency stable.
- Vector DB recommendation: managed vector DB for initial phase (reduces ops risk); fallback to self-hosted (Milvus/FAISS) for long-term cost evaluation. See tradeoffs in tab 3.

Ask from you for next step: can you share a short list (2–3) of high-traffic query groups and the current average query latency SLA? We’ll use those to size hot windows.

Attachments: NSH-implementation-map-v1.xlsx (implementation map)

Next steps proposed:
1) We deliver a prioritized backfill plan (by end of week)
2) Marissa to prototype rerank eval harness + sample dataset (rerank-eval-sample.jsonl)
3) We schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive for the infra/eng team to align on vector store API and metrics (suggest Thursday).

Thanks — Rishi

Thanks, Rishi — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying items from our side:

- NorthStar currently runs an ES-backed semantic layer with a FAISS sidecar for nightly embeddings; search users see 95th pctl latency ~220ms. We can tolerate short backfill windows if the front-end response stays under ~300ms.
- Our biggest concern is the initial coldstart for long-tail queries — we cannot accept a visible dip in precision for frequent user segments.

Specific asks:
1) What does an "incremental prioritization by traffic slice" look like in practice (a calendar or rollout table)?
2) What managed vector DBs do you recommend for minimal ops overhead but still good throughput (we currently use GCP gen2 infra)?
3) For rerank evals: do you provide an offline harness we can run in our environment, and what sample size do you recommend?

We’ll prepare the traffic slice list by end of day tomorrow. Samir and I are available for the deep-dive Thursday afternoon if that works.

Subject: Re: Implementation navigation: incremental embeddings backfill + rerank evaluation

Hi Ellie / Samir —

Thanks for sharing the latency target — that helps a lot. To answer your questions and make the plan concrete:

1) Rollout cadence (proposal):
   - Week 0: Export snapshot + seed hot index (top 5% queries by volume) -> warm prefix cache.
   - Week 1–2: Incremental backfill batch jobs (daily, prioritized by customer and query group). Monitor delta in latency and NDCG on a synthetic holdout.
   - Week 3: Canary rerank on 5% of traffic (A/B with traffic splitting by user-agent or header).
   - Week 4: Expand to 25% if metrics stable; full cutover week 6.

2) Vector DB options (short):
   - Pinecone (managed): fastest path, strong throughput, multi-region. Ops overhead minimal. Good for initial canary.
   - Milvus (self-hosted): lower unit cost at scale, needs ops for sharding/replicas. Consider if NSH wants on-prem or VPC control.
   - Redis Vector / Vearch: viable for low-dim fast lookups but less feature-rich for complex ANN configs.

Recommendation: start with Pinecone in us-central (GCP) for the canary, measure QPS and cost per query; evaluate Milvus on a small cluster for long-term TCO.

3) Rerank evals / sample size:
   - We’ll provide an offline harness (python script + sample jsonl) that computes NDCG@k, MRR, and regression counts.
   - Suggested experiment sizes: 10k labeled query-candidate pairs for a meaningful NDCG estimate; if labeling is expensive, use a seeded blind click-simulated holdout of ~50k to estimate online lifts.
   - Acceptance criteria (draft): NDCG@10 lift >= 0.08 vs baseline AND <1% severe regressions on core query bucket.

Attached: rerank-eval-sample.jsonl (sample lines and expected harness output), backfill-priority-matrix.csv (template).

Operational notes: keep a hot prefix (top-percentile keys) in the vector store and archive the rest to a cold embedding store (S3 + index hydration job) — this avoids indexing everything at once and keeps latency predictable.

Happy to walk through the implementation map on Thursday.

— Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — couple of technical clarifications from our infra team:

- Dimensionality: we currently use 1536-d embeddings. Are there any kernel-level implications for quantization (INT8/INT4) that would impact recall for rare queries?
- Distance metric: we want to keep cosine. Is the recommended flow cosine -> dot-product normalize? Any pitfalls for mixed metrics across candidate and rerank model?
- Batching / throughput: during canary we expect bursts up to 300 QPS. What throughput have you seen with Pinecone defaults for 1536-d cosine?
- Fallback plan: we’d like an explicit fallback to BM25 for the first-minute post-backfill on any failed ANN lookup. Any guidance on that pattern?

If you can share the harness and a short README on how to run it inside our CI, we’ll run it against our 10k-sample set.

— Samir
Senior ML Engineer, NorthStar Health

Ellie / Samir —

Great questions. Quick responses and an actionable schedule below. I’ll bring Marissa and Naomi to the technical deep-dive on Thursday at 2pm PT.

Answers:
- Quantization: INT8 is commonly used for production FAISS/Pinecone indexes with minimal recall loss for 1536-d vectors when you calibrate per-shard. We will run a small quantization sensitivity test on 1k holdout samples (Marissa to own).
- Cosine: keep cosine. Our routing normalizes vectors before ANN lookup so dot-product in the vector DB is equivalent to cosine. The main pitfall is mixing an unnormalized reranker input; ensure the reranker receives the original dense representations or normalized candidate vectors consistently.
- Throughput: with Pinecone standard configs we’ve observed sustained 200–400 QPS for 1536-d with sharding and async batching; your 300 QPS burst is within an expected canary shape but we’ll size headroom for 2x.
- Fallback: implement a short-circuit where a failed or slow ANN lookup (>250ms) falls back to BM25 results for that request. Log those events and surface as a rollback trigger.

Proposed concrete schedule (finalized at Thursday deep-dive):
- Wed 6/16: we deliver prioritized backfill CSV + runnable harness in the linked Drive.
- Thu 6/17 14:00 PT: tech deep-dive (Rishi/Marissa/Naomi + NSH infra).
- Week of 6/21: seed hot index, run quantization sensitivity tests, and run offline rerank evaluation on your 10k sample.
- Week of 6/28: canary (5% traffic) with detailed observability (per-token latency, NDCG, regressions).

Owners:
- Backfill plan & sequencing: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.com)
- Rerank harness & sensitivity tests: Naomi Feldman (naomi_feldman@redwood.com)
- Eng liaison / escalation: Rishi Malhotra (rishi@redwood.com)

If this looks good I’ll post the calendar invite and push the Drive folder to your org. We’ll also add the HubSpot deal note (NS-2026-0427) with acceptance criteria and rollback conditions.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.
